boxed_warning: WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY - When pregnancy is detected, discontinue ZESTRIL as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.
indications_and_usage: ZESTRIL is an angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor indicated for: Treatment of hypertension in adult patients and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older; Adjunctive therapy in heart failure in patients not responding adequately to diuretics and digitalis; Treatment of acute myocardial infarction within 24 hours of onset.
dosage_and_administration: Hypertension: Initial adult dose is 10 mg once daily. Dosage may be adjusted up to 40 mg daily based on clinical response. Heart failure: Initial dose 5 mg once daily with diuretics. Target dose is 20 to 40 mg once daily.
contraindications: ZESTRIL is contraindicated in patients with a history of angioedema related to previous ACE inhibitor treatment, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, and concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes.
warnings_and_cautions: Angioedema and Anaphylactoid Reactions: Discontinue ZESTRIL immediately. Impaired Renal Function: Monitor serum creatinine. Hyperkalemia: Monitor serum potassium periodically.
adverse_reactions: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%) are headache, dizziness, dry cough, postural effects, and diarrhea.
drug_interactions: Dual inhibition of renin-angiotensin system with ARBs or aliskiren increases hypotension and hyperkalemia risk. NSAIDs may diminish antihypertensive effect. Lithium toxicity may increase with concomitant ACE inhibitor use.

boxed_warning: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS - Post-marketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias. Assess renal function prior to initiation.
indications_and_usage: GLUCOPHAGE is a biguanide indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and pediatric patients 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_and_administration: Starting dose: 500 mg orally twice daily or 850 mg once daily with meals. Increase in increments of 500 mg weekly or 850 mg every 2 weeks up to maximum recommended dose of 2550 mg per day.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2). Known hypersensitivity to metformin. Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis.
warnings_and_cautions: Lactic acidosis: Assess patients with metabolic acidosis promptly. Vitamin B12 deficiency: Monitor hematologic parameters annually.
adverse_reactions: Most common adverse reactions (>5%) are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal bloating, flatulence, and anorexia.

indications_and_usage: LIPITOR is indicated as an adjunct to diet to reduce elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apo B, and triglycerides in patients with primary hyperlipidemia and to reduce the risk of MI and stroke in patients with cardiovascular disease.
dosage_and_administration: Starting dose: 10 to 20 mg once daily. Daily dose range: 10 to 80 mg once daily. Individualize according to target lipid goals.
contraindications: Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of hepatic transaminases. Hypersensitivity to any component. Pregnancy and lactation.
warnings_and_cautions: Myopathy and Rhabdomyolysis: Discontinue if markedly elevated CPK levels occur. Monitor liver enzymes before initiating therapy.
adverse_reactions: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%) are nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, pain in extremity, and urinary tract infection.
drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase atorvastatin plasma concentration and rhabdomyolysis risk. Fibrates and cyclosporine also increase myopathy risk.
